(b) Server Threats   Server threats in e -commerce refer to the various security risks and attacks that target web servers hosting  online business applications and data. Since servers store critical business and customer information, they  are primary targets for malicious attac ks.

Common server threats include the following. First, Denial of Service (DoS) attacks flood the server with  excessive requests, making it unavailable to legitimate users. Second, Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS)  attacks use multiple systems simultaneousl y to overwhelm the server. Third, unauthorized access occurs  when hackers exploit vulnerabilities to gain control of the server. Fourth, data theft involves stealing

sensitive customer data, financial records, and business information stored on the server.   Other server threats include SQL injection, where malicious code is inserted into database queries to  manipulate or extract data. Buffer overflow attacks exploit programming errors to crash the server or  execute unauthorized commands. Malware and viruses c an infect server software, corrupting data or  creating backdoors for attackers.

To protect servers, organizations implement firewalls, intrusion detection systems, regular security  patches, data encryption, and access control mechanisms. Server security is a critical component of any e - commerce security strategy, as a compromised serv er can lead to massive financial losses, legal liability,  and permanent damage to business reputation. (iv) EDI   [Same as 2022 Dec answer above - approximately 200 words]   Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) is the computer -to-computer exchange of standard business documents  between organizations. Instead of mailing paper purchase orders, invoices, or shipping documents,  companies using EDI send these documents electronically in a standardized format that can be processed

automatically by the receiving computer system.   EDI significantly reduces the time and cost associated with manual document processing. Benefits include reduced costs, faster order cyc les, improved inventory management, fewer errors, and  stronger business relationships.
